Studio / Privacy

Privacy

PicturaAI has no accounts, sets no cookies and does not track you. When it can, it paints your photo on your own device. This page explains exactly what happens to your photos and your data.

Last updated 16 November 2026

The short version

  • On most computers and recent phones, your photo is painted in your browser and never leaves your device.
  • On devices that can’t do that, when painting on the device fails, and in one “Describe it” case explained below, a smaller copy of your photo is sent to our server and painted there. The result is kept for about an hour (at most 70 minutes) and then deleted. The photo itself is never saved there.
  • Paintings you save to “My gallery” are kept only in your browser, on your device.
  • No sign-up, no cookies, no advertising, and we don’t sell or share data.

Your photos

Painted on your device

When your browser supports it (WebGL 2), the studio downloads the painting model once and runs it in your browser. Your photo, the result, the intensity slider, “Colours only”, “Paint a region”, “Style the subject” and “Animate” all work on your device. Nothing about the photo is sent to us. The studio tells you which mode it is using under its heading. The one exception, even on a device that can paint by itself, is a “Describe it” style that could not be looked up in advance (see “Describe it” below).

Painted on our server

On older devices, if painting on the device fails (or failed recently), or for the “Describe it” case below, the studio sends the photo to our server instead. Before it is sent, it is scaled down to at most 1024 pixels on the long side. If you use a painting of your own as the style, that painting is sent too, scaled to at most 512 pixels.

The server paints the picture in memory and sends it straight back. The photo you sent is not written to disk. The painted result is stored on the server under a random identifier for about an hour, so that it can be downloaded again, and is then deleted automatically: a clean-up runs every ten minutes and removes results older than an hour, so none is kept longer than about 70 minutes. It is never listed anywhere or used for anything else, and it is not used to train any model.

Region masks and adjustments

Brushed regions, intensity changes, colour-only transfers, animations and downloads are made in your browser in both modes. They are not sent to us.

“Describe it”

When you describe a style in words, the text you type (up to 200 characters) is sent to our server. If image generation is switched on, the server forwards it to Cloudflare Workers AI, which generates a small picture of the style and sends it back; Cloudflare handles the text under its own privacy policy. If generation is off or unavailable, the server matches your words to the closest painting in the collection. A generated style or a matched painting is then painted like any other, on your device when it can.

If our server can’t answer the request at all (for example while it is waking up, or when it is busy) and your browser can’t match your words to a painting by itself, the studio keeps your words selected instead. When you then paint, your photo (scaled down as described above) and your words are sent to our server together; the server matches the words to the closest painting and paints the picture there, even on a device that could paint by itself. We don’t store what you type. The server only counts how many pictures were generated each day, without the text.

What is stored on your device

PicturaAI sets no cookies. It uses your browser’s own storage for these things, which never leave your device:

  • My gallery (IndexedDB): paintings you choose to save, with your photo so you can keep editing them. Delete them one by one or with “Clear my gallery”.
  • Painting engine files (Cache Storage and IndexedDB): the model files and preset style data, so the studio starts faster next time.
  • Device settings (localStorage): the picture size your device handles well, and a note if painting on this device failed recently.

Clearing this site’s data in your browser settings removes all of it.

What our server and host record

The site runs on Render, which routes traffic through Cloudflare. Like almost every website, the server and the host keep technical logs of requests: your IP address, the time, and the address requested. We use them only to keep the service running and to find faults, and Render keeps them for a limited time under its own policy.

To stop any one visitor from overloading the free server, we count requests per IP address over short windows (for example, at most 10 server paintings a minute). These counters are kept in memory only and disappear when the server restarts.

Other services your browser contacts

  • Google Fonts serves the two typefaces. Your browser requests them from Google, which receives your IP address as part of that request.
  • jsDelivr serves the MediaPipe library behind “Style the subject” and “Style the background”. It is only downloaded when you use one of them. TensorFlow.js and the painting model come from our own server.

Two optional services can be switched on by whoever runs the site. When they are off, as they are by default, your browser is not allowed to contact them at all:

  • Cloudflare Web Analytics counts page views without cookies and without building a profile of you.
  • Sentry receives error reports (the error message, the page and your browser type) so bugs can be fixed. Server error reports exclude request bodies, IP addresses and other personal data. Your photos are never included.

Your choices

Because there are no accounts and we keep nothing that identifies you, there is no profile to download or delete. You can remove everything PicturaAI stores on your device by clearing the site’s data in your browser. Server results are deleted automatically after about an hour (at most 70 minutes).

Questions

PicturaAI is an open-source project. You can read exactly what the code does, or ask a question, on GitHub. If this policy changes, the date at the top of this page changes too.
